target: Hij weet niet hoe de vork in de steel zit.
english: He doesn't know how things really are.
old: 'Hoe de vork in de steel zit' = how things really stand.
focus: Give the literal image: 'hoe de vork in de steel zit' = literally how the fork sits in its handle = how things really stand.

target: Zij slaagt erin om alles op tijd klaar te krijgen.
english: She manages to get everything ready on time.
old: 'Erin slagen om te' = to manage to/succeed in.
focus: The anticipatory 'er': slagen in → erin slagen. 'Zij slaagt erin om ... te krijgen' = she succeeds in getting it done. Plain words.

target: Hij kwam naar Nederland om te studeren.
english: He came to the Netherlands to study.
old: Short 'om te' – purpose of coming.
focus: Clean first example of purpose 'om te' = in order to: 'om te studeren' = in order to study. Drop the odd 'Short' hook.

target: Zij stelt het op prijs als je niet om de hete brij draait.
english: She appreciates it if you don't beat around the bush.
old: 'Om de hete brij draaien' = to beat around the bush.
focus: Literal image: 'om de hete brij draaien' = circle around the hot porridge = beat around the bush. Quote the phrase.

target: Hij staat met zijn mond vol tanden van verbazing.
english: He is lost for words with amazement.
old: 'Met de mond vol tanden staan' = to be speechless.
focus: Literal image: 'met de mond vol tanden staan' = stand with your mouth full of teeth = be lost for words. Quote the phrase.

target: Wij zitten met de handen in het haar over dit probleem.
english: We are at our wits' end about this problem.
old: 'Met de handen in het haar zitten' = to be at a loss.
focus: Literal image: 'met de handen in het haar zitten' = sit with your hands in your hair = be at your wits' end. Quote the phrase.

target: Hoe dat precies is gebeurd, heeft niemand ooit begrepen.
english: How exactly that happened, no one has ever understood.
old: Indirect question in P1: verb-final in the embedded clause, inversion in main.
focus: A whole embedded clause in first position still forces V2: quote 'Hoe dat precies is gebeurd, heeft niemand' – the finite verb 'heeft' comes before the subject. Kill the 'P1' jargon.

target: He maat, heb je zin om vanavond langs te komen?
english: Hey buddy, do you feel like coming over tonight?
old: 'Zin hebben om' means 'to feel like doing something' – very informal.
focus: Quote 'heb je zin om ... langs te komen': zin hebben om + te + infinitive = to feel like doing something, an everyday phrase. Drop the inaccurate 'very informal'.

target: Niet alleen spreekt zij vloeiend Frans, maar ook Duits.
english: Not only does she speak fluent French, but also German.
old: 'Niet alleen...maar ook' triggers inversion in the first clause.
focus: Quote 'Niet alleen spreekt zij': fronting 'niet alleen' forces verb before subject, exactly like English 'Not only does she speak'. Contrastive-with-English angle; drop 'P1'.

target: Hoeveel het ook kost, we moeten dit project voltooien.
english: No matter how much it costs, we must complete this project.
old: 'Hoeveel...ook' is a concessive clause – main clause follows with inversion.
focus: Quote 'Hoeveel het ook kost': question word + ook = 'no matter how...'; same mold as wie dan ook, hoe dan ook. Drop the 'inversion' jargon framing.

target: De wouden fluisterden van vergane glorie en verloren dromen.
english: The forests whispered of bygone glory and lost dreams.
old: 'Vergane glorie' – literary alliterative phrase meaning 'bygone glory'.
focus: 'vergane glorie' is a fixed expression for bygone/faded glory, used of things past their prime. Drop the false 'alliterative' claim (v and g don't alliterate).

target: Immers, de waarheid laat zich niet in woorden vangen.
english: After all, the truth cannot be captured in words.
old: 'Immers' is literary connector; 'laat zich niet vangen' = reflexive impossibility.
focus: One rule only: quote 'de waarheid laat zich niet in woorden vangen' – laten + zich + infinitive = 'can(not) be Xed' (reflexive passive). Drop the second 'immers' point.

target: Pas als de zon schijnt, komen de toeristen naar het strand.
english: Only when the sun shines do the tourists come to the beach.
old: 'Pas als' restrictive temporal in P1 – main clause inverts.
focus: Fronted 'Pas als de zon schijnt' forces the verb ahead of the subject: 'komen de toeristen', not 'de toeristen komen' – English keeps SV.

target: Hoe langer je wacht, hoe moeilijker het wordt.
english: The longer you wait, the harder it becomes.
old: 'Hoe...hoe' comparative correlation – both clauses have verb-final order.
focus: 'Hoe langer..., hoe moeilijker...' = 'the longer..., the harder...'; both halves push their verb to the end (wacht, wordt).

target: Naarmate de dag vorderde, werd het steeds warmer.
english: As the day progressed, it grew warmer.
old: 'Naarmate' progressive clause – 'steeds + comparative' shows gradual change.
focus: 'steeds + comparative' = more and more: 'steeds warmer' = warmer and warmer / increasingly warm.

target: Nauwelijks waren we aangekomen toen het begon te onweren.
english: We had hardly arrived when it started to thunder.
old: 'Nauwelijks...toen' – literary construction triggering inversion.
focus: Fronted 'Nauwelijks' inverts to 'waren we aangekomen' – mirrors English 'Hardly had we arrived'.

target: De Deltacommissaris heeft geadviseerd dat de zeewering met twee meter verhoogd dient te worden.
english: The Delta Commissioner has advised that the seawall needs to be raised by two meters.
old: 'Dient te worden' – formal modal passive: 'dienen' (to ought) + 'te worden' + past participle.
focus: 'dienen te' = a formal, official 'must/should'; here in passive: 'dient te worden verhoogd' = must be raised.

target: De vlam der hoop flakkerde nog in de harten der bevolking.
english: The flame of hope still flickered in the hearts of the population.
old: 'Der' used twice – literary genitive; 'flakkeren' = to flicker.
focus: 'der' = archaic genitive 'of the': 'de vlam der hoop' = the flame of hope; modern Dutch uses 'van de'.

target: Na het eten doen we samen de afwas, dat hoort zo.
english: After eating, we do the dishes together, that's how it should be.
old: Dutch communal approach to chores – 'dat hoort zo' = that's proper.
focus: Idiom 'dat hoort zo' literally 'that belongs so' = 'that's how it should be / that's proper'; quote dat hoort zo.

target: De oude visser wiens verhalen legendarisch waren, zat elke avond op dezelfde plek aan de haven.
english: The old fisherman whose stories were legendary sat every evening at the same spot by the harbor.
old: 'Wiens' genitive + literary setting + cultural maritime reference.
focus: 'wiens' = relative 'whose' for a masculine/neuter antecedent; quote 'wiens verhalen'.

target: Het begrip duurzaamheid heeft in de loop der tijd een bredere betekenis gekregen.
english: The concept of sustainability has acquired a broader meaning over time.
old: 'In de loop der tijd' – academic/literary for 'over time'.
focus: 'der' in 'in de loop der tijd' is a fossilized genitive = 'of the', surviving only in fixed phrases; quote de loop der tijd.

target: Het zij zo, we zullen ons aanpassen aan de nieuwe omstandigheden.
english: So be it, we will adapt to the new circumstances.
old: 'Het zij zo' literary/archaic + reflexive 'zich aanpassen' + formal register.
focus: 'zij' in 'het zij zo' is the archaic subjunctive of zijn = 'so be it'; same 'zij' in 'God zij dank'.

target: De bootjes in de grachten varen zo dicht langs elkaar dat je de gesprekken kunt volgen.
english: The boats in the canals sail so close together that you can follow the conversations.
old: Cultural canal boats + result clause 'zo...dat' construction.
focus: 'zo ... dat' = 'so ... that' result clause; quote 'zo dicht ... dat'.

target: Indien de omstandigheden het toelaten, zullen we de buitenactiviteiten hervatten.
english: If circumstances permit, we will resume the outdoor activities.
old: 'Indien' formal + compound 'buitenactiviteiten' + formal 'hervatten'.
focus: 'indien' = formal/written 'if', where 'als' is the everyday spoken word; quote Indien.

target: Hoe onwaarschijnlijk het verhaal ook mag klinken, het is van begin tot eind waar.
english: However unlikely the story may sound, it is true from beginning to end.
old: 'Hoe...ook' concessive + modal 'mag' + literary 'van begin tot eind'.
focus: 'hoe ... ook' = 'however / no matter how' concessive; quote 'Hoe onwaarschijnlijk ... ook'.
